narration:
Imagine running the company behind the AI boom, then your CEO resigns immediately.
In its latest quarter, data-center revenue reached $89 billion.
On November 12, Jensen Huang resigned as CEO and board member.
CFO Colette Kress became interim CEO while the board searches for a replacement.
It says operations and its roadmap continue uninterrupted.
But why does this chip company matter?
Training AI means repeating enormous amounts of math.
A CPU handles jobs one at a time.
A GPU splits related calculations across huge numbers
of threads and runs them in parallel.
That makes training faster,
and helps run the finished model when you ask a question.
Its bigger advantage is CUDA and its libraries,
which give developers tools to train models and connect many GPUs across many machines.
So the company wasn't just selling chips.
It built the software ecosystem that made them practical at scale.
And here's the turn:
this leadership change tests whether that system can outlast that recognisable face.
Follow the channel for the free guide,
and find our community link in the description.
The CEO changed overnight, but the AI machine still has to keep running.

research.summary: NVIDIA’s importance in AI comes from a combination of hardware and software: GPUs can perform large numbers of related calculations in parallel, while CUDA and its libraries let researchers and companies use that hardware for training and running AI models at scale. Jensen Huang’s November 12, 2026 resignation is therefore more than a leadership headline: it raises questions about succession at the company supplying much of the infrastructure behind the current AI buildout, even as NVIDIA says operations, customer commitments and its product roadmap will continue without interruption.

claims.claim: Jensen Huang co-founded NVIDIA in 1993. NVIDIA’s own timeline credits the company’s 1999 GPU invention, its 2006 CUDA platform, and the 2012 AlexNet breakthrough as major steps in its shift from graphics hardware toward accelerated computing and AI.
claims.source_title: NVIDIA History: Innovations Over the Years

claims.claim: A GPU is useful for AI because it can launch very large numbers of threads and execute many related calculations in parallel. NVIDIA’s CUDA documentation describes GPU work as kernels executed by many threads, often organized into millions of threads.

Many neural-network workloads can be expressed as matrix multiplication and other parallel operations. NVIDIA’s deep-learning performance documentation specifically identifies matrix multiplication, convolution and recurrent layers as operations that GPUs can accelerate through parallel computation.
claims.source_title: Get Started With Deep Learning Performance

claims.claim: NVIDIA’s advantage is not limited to chips. CUDA provides the programming layer, while CUDA-X and libraries such as cuDNN provide optimized building blocks for training and inference, including matrix multiplication, attention, convolution and normalization.

NVIDIA’s software stack is designed to connect with major AI frameworks and to scale from one GPU to multiple GPUs and multiple nodes. NVIDIA lists support for PyTorch, TensorFlow and JAX, while NCCL provides optimized communication for multi-GPU and multi-node systems.
NVIDIA’s second quarter of fiscal 2027, ended July 26, 2026, produced $96.2 billion in total revenue, including $89.0 billion in Data Center revenue, up 117% from the same quarter a year earlier.
claims.source_title: NVIDIA Announces Financial Results for Second Quarter Fiscal 2027

claims.claim: The leadership change creates a succession question because NVIDIA’s board said it is beginning a search for a permanent CEO and will consider both internal and external candidates. The board also said operations, customer commitments and the product roadmap are expected to continue without interruption.
Colette Kress became interim CEO while continuing as NVIDIA’s executive vice president and chief financial officer. She has served as NVIDIA’s CFO since joining the company in September 2013.

core_fact.fact: On November 12, 2026, NVIDIA announced that Jensen Huang had resigned immediately as president, CEO and a board member, and that CFO Colette Kress had become interim CEO while the board searched for a permanent successor.

metadata.description:
Free guide to this video (steps and every source): https://studio.golidee.com/guides/golide-short-2026-11-16.pdf

Jensen Huang has resigned as NVIDIA’s CEO and board member, with CFO Colette Kress stepping in as interim CEO. The leadership change comes as NVIDIA reports $89 billion in data-center revenue and remains central to the AI boom.

This short explains why NVIDIA’s GPUs, CUDA software, and developer ecosystem matter—and why the company’s biggest test may be whether its AI machine can keep running without its most recognizable leader.
